record.title: Algebraicity conjecture for Ramsey multiplicity constants
record.statement:
For graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$, let $c(H_1,H_2)$ denote their balanced Ramsey multiplicity constant.

**Algebraicity conjecture.** There do not exist graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ such that $c(H_1,H_2)$ is transcendental.

The conjecture asserts that every Ramsey multiplicity constant is algebraic, while allowing that some such constants may be irrational. No resolution is given here.
record.source_name: Elena Moss and Jonathan A. Noel, “Off-Diagonal Ramsey Multiplicity”, arXiv:2306.17388 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

record.title: Localization accessibility of Theorem summod5
record.statement: The localization method is applied to the functions and congruences described above, with $L_{\alpha}=L_{\alpha}^{(0)}+L_{\alpha}^{(1)}$ lying in $\mathcal{M}(\mathrm{X}_0(10))$ and satisfying $L_{\alpha}\equiv 0\pmod{5^{\alpha}}$. **Localization accessibility claim.** Theorem summod5 is accessible via the localization method. record.title: The treewidth formula for the fall-off value of graph polytopes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ denote its treewidth, and let $\tau(G)$ denote its fall-off value.

**Treewidth fall-off conjecture.** The fall-off value is

$$
\tau(G)=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tw}(G)+1}.
$$

The paper motivates this formula from the graphs analyzed, including trees, cyclic graphs, and graphs of treewidth two, but no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Addario-Berry–Havet–Linhares Sales–Thomassé–Reed antidirected tree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer.

**Addario-Berry–Havet–Linhares Sales–Thomassé–Reed conjecture.** If

$$
e(D)\geq (k-1)|V(D)|,
$$

then $D$ contains a copy of every antidirected tree with $k$ edges.

This is a directed analogue of the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The source introduces it as an open generalization for directed graphs.
record.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Hyperstability in the Erdős-Sós Conjecture”, arXiv:2409.15191 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

record.title: Aharoni-Berger strong conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $M_1,\dots,M_n$ be matchings of size $n+1$ in a bipartite graph. A **rainbow matching** is a matching whose edges can be assigned distinct indices $i$ so that each edge belongs to $M_i$.

**Aharoni-Berger strong conjecture.** Every collection of $n$ matchings of size $n+1$ in a bipartite graph admits a rainbow matching of size $n$.

The extra edge in each matching permits a full rainbow matching and implies the preceding bipartite $n-1$ conjecture by adjoining a common dummy edge. The bound $n+1$ is best possible, while the conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Candida Bowtell, Andrea Freschi, Gal Kronenberg and Jun Yan, “A note on improved bounds for hypergraph rainbow matching problems”, arXiv:2501.03216 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03216

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: Aharoni-Berger non-bipartite strong conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M_1,\dots,M_n$ be matchings of size $n+2$ in a graph. A **rainbow matching** is a matching whose edges can be assigned distinct indices $i$ so that each edge belongs to $M_i$.

**Aharoni-Berger non-bipartite strong conjecture.** Every collection of $n$ matchings of size $n+2$ in a graph admits a rainbow matching of size $n$.

The statement is the non-bipartite analogue of the preceding strong conjecture, with two additional edges required in each matching. It was implicitly made in the cited earlier work and stated explicitly in the source, with no resolution supplied here.
record.source_name: Candida Bowtell, Andrea Freschi, Gal Kronenberg and Jun Yan, “A note on improved bounds for hypergraph rainbow matching problems”, arXiv:2501.03216 (2025).

record.title: Burr–Erdős conjecture on Ramsey numbers of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices. **Burr–Erdős conjecture.**

$$
R(T,T) \leq 2n-2
$$

when $n$ is even, and

$$
R(T,T) \leq 2n-3
$$

otherwise.

This is a central conjecture in the study of Ramsey numbers of trees; the source presents it as a major conjecture without giving evidence of its resolution.
record.source_name: Yair Caro and Xandru Mifsud, “On zero-sum Ramsey numbers modulo 3”, arXiv:2502.03864 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03864

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2025). “Amongst the many open problems remaining concerning trees, we mention the following conjecture.”

record.title: Sign-change conjecture for Birch–Erdős representation functions
record.statement:
Let $f_{p,q}(n)$ be the Birch–Erdős representation function, with $p$ and $q$ relatively prime integers satisfying $q>p>2$. **Sign-change conjecture.** The sign of

$$
f_{p,q}(n+1)-f_{p,q}(n)
$$

changes infinitely often. The conjecture is presented as a possible example of the Chebyshev bias phenomenon; the source does not establish it.
record.source_name: Yuchen Ding, Honghu Liu and Zi Wang, “Note on a theorem of Birch and Erdős”, arXiv:2503.11676 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11676

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Erdős's clique-partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph on $n=km$ vertices. A partition of $V(H)$ into $k$ sets each inducing an $m$-clique is called a **$k$-partition into $m$-cliques**. **Erdős's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(H)\geq n\left(1-\frac{1}{m}\right),
$$

then $V(H)$ has a $k$-partition into $m$-cliques. This is equivalent to the equitable-coloring formulation below and was later proved by Hajnal and Szemerédi.
record.source_name: H. A. Kierstead, Alexandr Kostochka and Zimu Xiang, “Results and Problems on Equitable Coloring of Graphs”, arXiv:2504.14711 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14711

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Perfect-or-bounded-clique-width conjecture for claw-, $4K_1$-, and bridge-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $(claw, 4K_1, bridge)$-free graph.

**Perfect-or-bounded-clique-width conjecture.** One of the following holds:

- $G$ is perfect.
- $G$ has bounded clique-width.

The conjecture would remove the $C_4$-twin restriction from the paper's polynomial-time colouring result by establishing bounded clique-width whenever such a graph is not perfect. Its status is open in the source.
record.source_name: Kathie Cameron, Chính T. Hoàng and Taite LaGrange, “On graphs without four-vertex induced subgraphs”, arXiv:2505.00202 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00202

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

record.title: Erdős's conjecture on 5-cycles in triangle-free graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices. **Erdős's conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains at most $(n/5)^5$ cycles of length $5$. The balanced blow-up of the $5$-cycle $C_5$ attains this bound when $n$ is divisible by $5$, but the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Jorik Jooken, “Computer-assisted graph theory: a survey”, arXiv:2508.20825 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20825

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: Jain's $S^2$-flow conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph, and let $\phi_{3,2}(G)$ be its three-dimensional Euclidean flow index. **Jain's $S^2$-flow conjecture.**

$$
\phi_{3,2}(G)=2
$$

Equivalently, every bridgeless graph admits a unit-sphere flow in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The source states that this conjecture, together with Jain's $S^2$-map conjecture, would imply Tutte's $5$-flow conjecture; its resolution is not given.
record.source_name: Chenxing Li, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo and Bo Su, “High-Dimensional p-Normed Flows”, arXiv:2601.12036 (2026).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2510.22234](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22234), [arXiv:2510.19411](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19411), [arXiv:2304.14231](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.14231).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12036

record.title: The polynomial-time solvability conjecture for totally -modular integer programs
record.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ be a totally $\Delta$-modular matrix, meaning that every square submatrix of $A$ has determinant bounded by $\Delta$ in absolute value. For integer vectors $b,w$ and integer variable vector $x$, consider the integer program

$$
\max\{w^Tx: Ax \leq b,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}^n\}.
$$

**Totally $\Delta$-modular integer-program conjecture.** For any constant $\Delta$, this integer program can be solved in polynomial time when $A$ is totally $\Delta$-modular.

The case $\Delta=1$ is the totally unimodular case. Artmann, Weismantel, and Zenklusen answered the conjecture affirmatively for $\Delta=2$, while the cases $\Delta\geq 3$ remain open.
record.source_name: Caleb McFarland, “Totally Δ-Modular Tree Decompositions of Graphic Matrices for Integer Programming”, arXiv:2602.01499 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01499

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2026). “Artmann, Weismantel, and Zenklusen answered the conjecture in the affirmative for $\Delta = 2$, but $\Delta \geq 3$ remains open.”

record.title: Canonical vertex-Ramsey characterization of the finite sunflower property
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a relational Fraïssé class with strong amalgamation. The **canonical vertex-Ramsey characterization.**

$$
\mathcal{K}\text{ has the canonical vertex-Ramsey property}\iff\mathcal{K}\text{ has the finite sunflower property}.
$$

The source also conjectures that having the finite $2$-sunflower property is equivalent to having the finite sunflower property; it notes that the displayed equivalence would imply this. The question concerns whether the finite sunflower property admits a characterization analogous to that of the infinite sunflower property.
record.source_name: Rob Sullivan and Jeroen Winkel, “Structured sunflowers and canonical Ramsey properties”, arXiv:2602.04610 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

record.title: Bobby's spherical flow conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. An **$\mathbb{S}^2$-flow** is a unit vector flow with values on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$. **Bobby's spherical flow conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has an $\mathbb{S}^2$-flow. This conjecture is proposed as one of two conjectures intended to imply Tutte's $5$-flow conjecture; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Hussein Houdrouge, Bobby Miraftab and Pat Morin, “2-dimensional unit vector flows”, arXiv:2602.21526 (2026).

record.title: The tangled-cord extremal conjecture for Hamiltonian sets in simple assembly graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a simple assembly graph with $n$ rigid vertices, each of degree $4$, and let $F_k$ denote the $k$th Fibonacci number. A **Hamiltonian set of polygonal paths** is a Hamiltonian set as defined for such assembly graphs. **Tangled-cord extremal conjecture.** The upper bound for the maximal number of Hamiltonian sets of polygonal paths is

$$
F_{2n+1}-1.
$$

This bound is achieved only by the tangled cord with $n$ rigid vertices of degree $4$. Earlier work established the upper bound and showed that it is tight; the conjecture concerns the uniqueness of the extremal graph, and the present paper develops equivalent combinatorial conditions intended to prove it.
record.source_name: A. Guterman, N. Jonoska, E. Kreines, A. Maksaev and N. Ostroukhova, “Hamiltonian Sets of Polygonal Paths in Assembly Graphs”, arXiv:2603.07296 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07296

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: Wu–Magnant–Nowbandegani–Xia conjecture for multicolor Ramsey numbers of cherries
record.statement:
Let $k,n_1,\ldots,n_k$ be positive integers, and let $n=\max\{n_1,\ldots,n_k\}$. Here $P_3$ is the path on three vertices, also called a cherry, and $R(n_1P_3,\ldots,n_kP_3)$ denotes the $k$-color Ramsey number for vertex-disjoint unions of the indicated numbers of cherries.

**Wu–Magnant–Nowbandegani–Xia conjecture.**

$$
R(n_1P_3,\ldots,n_kP_3)=2n+\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_i-k+1.
$$

The formula is known to be a general lower bound, arising from the standard construction for multicolor matching Ramsey numbers. The conjecture asserts that this lower bound is always tight; the general multicolor case remains open.
record.source_name: Yanbo Zhang, Qian Chen and Yaojun Chen, “Ramsey numbers and Gallai–Ramsey numbers of disjoint unions of cherries”, arXiv:2605.02793 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02793

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

record.title: Erdős–Rubin–Taylor conjecture on planar graph choosability
record.statement: A **planar graph** is a graph that can be drawn in the plane without crossings. **Erdős–Rubin–Taylor's conjecture.** Every planar graph is 5-choosable. Since planar graphs are 5-degenerate, they are immediately 6-choosable; the conjecture was later proved by Thomassen, who established the stronger 5-choosability result.
record.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: List Total Coloring Conjecture
record.statement:
For a multigraph $G$, a **total coloring** colors vertices and edges so that adjacent vertices, incident edges, and incident vertex-edge pairs receive distinct colors. Let $\chi”(G)$ be the total chromatic number and $\chi”_\ell(G)$ the list total chromatic number. **List Total Coloring Conjecture.** For any multigraph $G$,

$$
\chi”_\ell(G)=\chi”(G).
$$

The conjecture is known for several classes, including multigraphs whose underlying simple graph is a forest or circuit and bipartite graphs with total chromatic number $\Delta+2$; no general resolution is given.
record.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).

record.title: Van der Holst's classification of the obstructions to Colin de Verdière invariant at most 5
record.statement:
Let $\mu(G)$ denote the Colin de Verdière invariant of a graph $G$. The $K_7$ and $K_{3,3,1,1}$ families are the graph families generated by the indicated germs under the relevant $\nabla\mathrm{Y}$ operations.

**Van der Holst's classification conjecture.** The graphs in the $K_7$ and $K_{3,3,1,1}$ families are the obstructions to $\mu\leq 5$.

This proposed classification concerns the minor obstructions for the Colin de Verdière invariant bound $\mu\leq 5$. The source presents it as a proposal and does not state that it has been proved or disproved.
